thread:
marie: Quick thread — regression observed after 1.2.3 rollout: stream tail latency for small-token responses spikes ~2-4x when continuous batching is enabled with default token budget. Posting profiler + KV stats here.

bench-bot: benchmark-run:1756004300 finished — baseline(1.2.2) 99p=240ms, canary(1.2.3) 99p=980ms :sad-panda:

akash: Can you paste the pprof/top and any kv hit rates?

marie: pprof snapshot from canary (short):
```
pprof top
flat  cum   self  name
0.32  1.20  0.32  decode_partial_send
0.25  0.80  0.25  continuous_batch_coalesce
0.15  0.70  0.15  kv_warmup_block
0.10  0.30  0.10  kernel_select_sync
```

lin: KV metrics (same run):
- overall_kv_hit_rate: 0.78
- kv_hit_rate(seq_len<=8): 0.58  <-- big drop
- avg_kv_latency: 4.6ms (warm) -> 18.2ms (cold churn)

taylor: So small seqs are thrashing the KV warmup when we partial-decode+flush early?

marie: Exactly. We saw many tiny requests trigger partial-decode flushes (stream_flush_ms=20ms) which causes repeated KV fetches and forces kernel selection path to run under lock per partial. Token budget stays low so batches are tiny and we spin.

marie: Current batching config that triggered it:
```
batching:
  min_batch_tokens: 16
  token_budget_target: 96
  stream_flush_ms: 20
  partial_decode_preempt: true
```

akash: 20ms flush is aggressive for small payloads. We preempt decode and kick off kv fetch per partial -> thrash. Suggest: increase flush window for tiny requests and bump token_budget_target for tiny queue keys. Also consider kv_prefetch on admission for seq<=8.

marie: Trying an experiment now: rule -> if payload_tokens <= 8 then set stream_flush_ms=80, token_budget_target=128, kv_prefetch=true. Kicking off canary.

bench-bot: experiment-run:1756007500 results:
- 99p tail: 260ms (was 980ms)
- kv_hit_rate(seq_len<=8): 0.93
- kernel_select_sync time: negligible in top sample
Looks close to baseline.

lin: Nice. Two follow-ups: 1) prefer small-kernel variant for partial-decode path in kernel selector; 2) add per-queue aging weight so tiny requests don't starve or get endlessly coalesced/evicted.

akash: Also add metric partial_decode_requeue_count and partial_decode_preempt_count so we can alert on preempt thrash. Filing small PR to precompute kernel choice during admission to reduce kernel_select_sync lock time.

marie: I'll push a canary with the rule and kernel-selector precompute for 1 hour, then flip if stable. Note: quantized small kernels increase GPU memory slightly — watching dedicated pools.

taylor: I'll create an alert: rolling 99p > 500ms for 10m -> rollback. Also adding dashboard tile: KV hit rate by seq_len bucket + partial_decode_requeue metric.

akash: One more optimization idea: when we detect stream client is waiting and seq_len small, delay flush until either token_budget_target or flush_ms threshold OR kv_prefetch completes. That avoids partial sends that cause extra KV fetches.

marie: Good idea — add as follow-up. TL;DR: root cause = small-payload streaming + aggressive flush + low token budget -> KV warmup thrash + kernel-select stalls. Quick mitigation = bump flush window for tiny payloads, raise token budget, enable kv_prefetch. Canary looks good so far. :thumbsup:
